session.about: Manage chat sessions: create, send, open, list, get, rename, move, move to group, clear project, fork, archive

create.about: Create a new chat session and send a prompt in it (fire-and-forget)
create.afterHelp:
Examples:
  berdctl session create --prompt "Triage the failing nightly build" \
    --harness-id claude-acp --from "the release orchestrator" --json
  berdctl session create --prompt "Implement the fix" \
    --project-id <project-id> --startup-name my-feature

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "harness_id": "...",
   "send_status": "dispatched"}
  The session runs in the background; the user's view does not change. Check
  progress later with `berdctl session get --session-id <session_id>`.

send.about: Send a prompt into an existing chat session
send.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session send --session-id <session-id> \
    --prompt "Check the latest CI failure" --if-running queue \
    --from "the Berd session handling CI" --delivery-id <stable-id> --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "send_status": "dispatched"|"steered"|"queued"|"deduplicated"}
  The user's current view does not change.

open.about: Open a session in the app window the user is looking at
open.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session open --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the session is now on screen.

list.about: List the user's chat sessions (most recent first)
list.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session list --query "review" --limit 10 --json

Result:
  {"sessions": [{"session_id": "...", "title": "...",
                 "project_id": "..."|null, "updated_at": "...",
                 "is_running": false, "chat_state": "idle",
                 "message_count": 12}, ...]}
  Most recent first; archived sessions are excluded.

get.about: Read one session's metadata and optionally its latest messages
get.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session get --session-id <session-id> --messages 5 --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "harness_id": "...",
   "model_id": "..."|null, "agent_id": "..."|null,
   "project_id": "..."|null, "working_dir": "..."|null,
   "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "...", "archived": false,
   "is_running": false, "is_open_in_window": false,
   "chat_state": "idle", "message_count": 12,
   "messages": [{"role": "user"|"assistant"|null, "text": "..."}, ...]}
  "messages" is present only when --messages > 0; each message text is
  truncated to 2000 chars.

rename.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session rename --session-id <session-id> --title "CI triage"

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the new title appears immediately in the app's session list.

move.about: Move a chat session into a project
move.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session move --session-id <session-id> --project-id <project-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the app's session list regroups immediately.

move-to-group.about: Move a chat session into an existing project group
move-to-group.afterHelp:
Find the destination group id with:
  berdctl project get --project-id <project-id> --json

Example:
  berdctl session move-to-group --session-id <session-id> \
    --group-id <group-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true, "project_id": "...", "group_id": "...",
   "group_name": "..."} — the project chat list regroups immediately.

clear-project.about: Move a chat session out of any project
clear-project.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session clear-project --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the app's session list regroups immediately.

fork.about: Fork a chat session into an independent copy with its history
fork.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session fork --session-id <session-id> --title "Alternate approach"

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "source_session_id": "...",
   "message_count": 7}
  The fork appears in the session list with a copy of the original history.

archive.about: Archive a chat and clean up its Goose-managed Git resources
archive.afterHelp:
By default, the command refuses to archive when Git cleanup would discard local files or changes.
Use --discard-changes to allow that loss. The command never opens an interactive prompt.

Examples:
  berdctl session archive --session-id <session-id>
  berdctl session archive --session-id <session-id> --discard-changes

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the session was archived and eligible worktrees and branches were removed.

folder.about: Manage attached chat folders: attach, detach, replace, set cwd, list

attach.about: Attach a folder, repository, or worktree to a chat
attach.afterHelp:
Use this after creating or adopting a folder inside a workspace root already authorized for the chat. Registered Git worktrees of an authorized repository are also allowed; select a new unrelated root in Berd first.

Example:
  berdctl folder attach --session-id <session-id> --path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null}

detach.about: Detach a folder, repository, or worktree from a chat
detach.afterHelp:
Detach the checked-out folder to detach its branch from chat context. This does not delete anything from disk or Git.

Example:
  berdctl folder detach --session-id <session-id> --path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "detached": true|false}

replace.about: Replace the chat's current folder with another
replace.afterHelp:
Prefer this over set-cwd when the user says to switch or move the chat to a new worktree/folder and does not ask to retain the old folder as context. Use set-cwd to select an already attached folder or when the old attachment should remain.

The old path must be attached. For the usual switch flow, get the current cwd from `berdctl folder list` and pass it as --old-path.

Example:
  berdctl folder replace --session-id <session-id> --old-path ~/src/repo --new-path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "oldPath": "...", "newPath": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null}

set-cwd.about: Select a chat folder as cwd, retaining other attachments
set-cwd.afterHelp:
For a request to switch or move the chat to a new worktree/folder, prefer `folder replace` so the old folder leaves context. Use this command when selecting among attachments or intentionally retaining the old folder.

The path must satisfy the same authorization rules as folder attach. Files and Git state are not moved.

Example:
  berdctl folder set-cwd --session-id <session-id> --path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null, "status": "applied"|"pending"}

list.about: List folders attached to a chat and identify its cwd
list.afterHelp:
The top-level cwd is returned even when it is Berd's implicit default and is not an attached folder.

Example:
  berdctl folder list --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true, "cwd": "...", "folders": [{"path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null, "cwd": true|false}]}

project.about: Manage projects: create, list, get, attach folder, detach folder, set startup mode, archive

create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl project create --name "Code reviews" \
    --instructions "Prefer small diffs" \
    --working-dir /Users/me/src/api --working-dir /Users/me/src/web

Result:
  {"project_id": "..."} — the project appears immediately in the app's
  project list with both directories attached.

attach-folder.about: Attach a folder to an existing project
attach-folder.afterHelp:
The new folder starts with startup mode "none"; set worktree behavior with
`berdctl project set-startup-mode` afterwards. Detach with
`berdctl project detach-folder`.

Example:
  berdctl project attach-folder --project-id <project-id> --path ~/src/api

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null,
   "attached": true, "working_dirs": ["...", ...]}

detach-folder.about: Detach a folder from an existing project
detach-folder.afterHelp:
Sessions already in the project keep their own folders; this only changes which
folders new project chats start from. Re-add with
`berdctl project attach-folder`.

Example:
  berdctl project detach-folder --project-id <project-id> --path ~/src/api

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "detached": true|false, "working_dirs": [...]}

set-startup-mode.about: Set how a project's new chats start from its Git workspaces

archive.about: Archive a project (reversible; nothing is deleted)
archive.afterHelp:
Archiving is reversible from the app's archive view; nothing is
deleted, and the project's sessions are left untouched.

Example:
  berdctl project archive --project-id <project-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the project disappears from the app's project list.

create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl agent create --name "Reviewer" \
    --system-prompt "You review diffs for correctness; be terse."

Result:
  {"agent_id": "..."} — the agent is saved and becomes available in
  future chats; pass it as --agent-id to `berdctl session create`.

list.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl agent list --json

Result:
  {"agents": [{"agent_id": "...", "name": "...",
               "summary": "...", "builtin": false}, ...]}
  Use an agent_id as --agent-id when creating a session.

create.about: Create a new skill (saved as a SKILL.md)
create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl skill create --name "release-notes" \
    --description "Draft release notes from merged PRs" \
    --content "$(cat SKILL.md)"

Result:
  {"skill_id": "..."} — the skill is saved as a SKILL.md and auto-loads
  into future sessions.

list.about: List the user's skills (name and description only)
list.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl skill list --json

Result:
  {"skills": [{"skill_id": "...", "name": "...",
               "description": "...",
               "source": "app"|"builtin"|"global"|"project"}, ...]}
  Read a skill's full content with `berdctl skill get`.

get.about: Read one skill including its SKILL.md instructions

feedback.about: Open or submit an approved Berd feedback report

open.about: Open the feedback form with a report prefilled
open.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl feedback open --title "Composer loses draft" \
    --description "Steps to reproduce..." --include-logs --json

Result:
  {"opened":true,"include_logs":true} — the existing feedback form is visible
  for review and optional image attachments; nothing was submitted.

submit.about: Submit an approved report directly to the Berd team
submit.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl feedback submit --title "Composer loses draft" \
    --description "Steps to reproduce..." --include-logs --json

Result:
  {"submitted":true,"include_logs":true,"issue_url":"https://..."}
  issue_url is omitted when the feedback service does not return one.

info.about: Look up installed harnesses, available models, and the app context

harnesses.about: List the agent harnesses sessions can run on, with readiness
harnesses.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl info harnesses --json

Result:
  {"harnesses": [{"harness_id": "goose", "name": "...",
                  "is_default": true,
                  "status": "ready"|"not_installed"|"not_ready"}, ...]}
  Only "ready" harnesses accept new sessions; "not_installed" and
  "not_ready" (sign-in or setup required) need the user to fix them in
  the app first.

models.about: List the models available per agent harness
models.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl info models --harness-id goose --json

Result:
  {"harnesses": [{"harness_id": "...",
                  "models": [{"model_id": "...", "name": "...",
                              "provider": "..."?}],
                  "warning": "..."?}]}
  Use a model_id (with its harness) as --model-id when creating a session.
  "warning" appears when a stale cached list was served or when the harness
  manages its model outside the app.

context.about: Read what the user is looking at in the app right now
context.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl info context --json

Result:
  {"view": "...", "active_session_id": "..."|null,
   "active_project_id": "..."|null, "voice_session_active": true|false,
   "app_version": "..."}
